title: Declare each item's cueing intent
statement: State in each item's specification the cueing it intends (none, support, diagnostic or authentic), and treat any cue it doesn't declare as a defect.
detail: An assessment BrainLift holds that cueing is a design lever to name or eliminate: unnamed cueing leaks validity, deliberate cueing speeds diagnosis, and declaring the intent up front aligns an item's claims, scoring and feedback and prevents accidental narrowing of what it measures. It notes that difficulty and discrimination tend to shift after cue edits, and asks for a cueing-intent field in every specification and a cue sweep in review. A Grade 3 reading red-team standard adopts the rule as an item-construction criterion checked in human review: every item declares its cue intent, and residual cues are defects.
